LESSON: READING 4.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How would you use contextual clues to infer character traits of the characters in a short story? 2. Why is it important to retell a story one has read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the characters in a short story,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use contextual clues to infer character traits of the characters in a short story,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the role of characters in a short story. ● Guide the learners to read the short story and retell what they have read. ● Guide the learners to describe the traits of the characters in the short story using different adjectives. ● Guide the learners to compare and contrast the traits of the characters that appear in the short story. ● In groups, guide the learners to role play the different characters and discuss their importance in the short story. ● Let the learner make connections between their own lives and those of characters in the text. 1. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication: The learner discusses the character traits in the short story, thereby practising the skills of effective

communication in speaking.

● Collaboration: the learner collaborates with other learners in groups and recognises their importance during the role play.
